title: Ang 1351: Namdev and Beni
hook: the last Bhagats of the last full raga
tomorrow: one short raga is left after dawn. whose hymns are in it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, on ang 1349, Kabir at dawn: from one light the whole world welled up, so who is good and who is bad? First, the light. Today, the last page of the dawn raga.
screen: `FIRST, THE LIGHT.` → `THE DAWN RAGA'S LAST PAGE.`

segments.voice: Some profiles are all badges: the certificates, the volunteer hours, the photo at the right event. On ang 1351 there's a man like that, long before profiles. Sandalwood paste on his body, leaves on his forehead, every mark of a holy man. And then the hymn says it: in his heart, his hand holds a knife. Here's the odd part. This sharp little portrait is the last word of Prabhati, the dawn raga. Why end there?
screen: `ALL BADGES.` → `HOLY MARKS, A KNIFE INSIDE.` → `WHY END THE DAWN RAGA HERE?`

segments.voice: Start with the pattern. In each raga of the Granth, the Gurus' hymns come first, then the Bhagats: poet-saints from other backgrounds, Hindu and Muslim, whose words the Gurus kept. Prabhati ends that way: Kabir, then Namdev, then Beni. Namdev's hymn here turns inward. In paraphrase: the pain of the mind, only the mind knows; or tell it to the One who understands. Then Beni's portrait. The man has the paste and the marks. His eyes are a cheat's, Beni says, and he sits as still as a crane at the water's edge, very holy-looking, waiting for a fish. Spotless outside, hunting inside. Beni names it plainly and doesn't soften it. So why close the dawn raga on that? The Granth doesn't explain its order, and readers give their own answers. One comes from the hymns themselves. Dawn is waking up, and the raga's last page holds up a mirror. Namdev says the mind knows its own pain; Beni shows a man whose marks hide his heart. Both point the same way: inside. Another answer is simpler. These are the last Bhagats of the dawn raga, and the Gurus kept their voices whole, sharp edges included. Either way, the page asks the reader a question. What's under the marks?
screen: `GURUS FIRST, THEN THE BHAGATS.` · `NAMDEV: THE MIND KNOWS ITS PAIN.` · `BENI: THE CRANE AT THE WATER.` · `THE LAST PAGE IS A MIRROR.` · then, large: `THE LAST BHAGATS.`

segments.voice: Look at one thing you wear or carry that says something about you: a ring, a kara, a lanyard, a phone case. Keep your eyes on it through the sit. Ask it, quietly, what it says, and whether the inside says the same.
Ang 1351. The last page of Prabhati, where Namdev turns inward and Beni paints the man with marks outside and a knife within.
Carry this: the last bhagats, and a dawn raga that closes on a mirror, not a badge. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the Granth each raga gathers the Gurus' hymns first and the Bhagats' after; in Prabhati the Bhagats are Kabir, Namdev and Beni, and their hymns are sung in kirtan like the Gurus' own.

fork.setup: one club member wears every badge and never helps. another helps every week and wears nothing. a teacher asks you who the real member is. what does Beni's hymn point you to?
options: look past both outsides: Beni's question is what's in the heart, which badges can't show.
the one with no badges; Beni says anyone wearing marks must be faking it.
the one with badges; Beni's hymn is about knives, not about clubs.
fork.reveal: Beni doesn't say every marked person is a fake. he paints one whose marks hide a knife, and turns the question inward: what's under the marks?
